node.label: Matthew Frye Jacobson
node.date_label: Whiteness of a Different Color (1998) · Barbarian Virtues (2000) · Roots Too (2006)
node.description: A historian of race, migration and political culture in the United States. His written PBS interview explains how distinctions among European immigrants were once treated as racial differences and later reconfigured as ethnicity. He connects those changing categories to arguments about fitness for citizenship and self-government. The entry treats racial classifications as historical objects, retains the distinctions between scholarly claims and the categories of historical actors, and does not certify every example in the unread monographs.

hc171_bederman_extract.note: After the frozen 1.171 indexed/mediated check, the same public scan was successfully retrieved via its S3 CDN: https://s3.amazonaws.com/files.commons.gc.cuny.edu/wp-content/blogs.dir/4188/files/2018/08/Bederman-Manliness-and-Civilization.pdf . Printed pp. 4–9 and 42–43 were then read through page OCR; PDF page 3 (printed 2–3) visually inspected to confirm the two-page scan mapping. Pp. 5–8 define manhood as a historical process relating bodies, identities and authority; pp. 42–43 explain racial/civilizational strategies. P. 43 explicitly limits the selected cases to varied discursive positions rather than representativeness or measured effects on others. Full chapter/book and endnotes remain unread; historical examples are not independently checked. Earlier 403 and indexed/Harvey reading limits remain the historical scope of the earlier check; no claim or edge changes follow.
